final_material_defects.finding: The selected PowerSync transaction-grouping history is retained as a closed report without a visible closure explanation, although the same primary issue contains a February 12, 2024 maintainer explanation naming fixed RN SDK 1.2.1 and Web SDK 0.2.1.
final_material_defects.governing_obligation: Complete consequential issue/fix/release history and available mechanism research; unknown inspected source context must not substitute for an available governing explanation.
final_material_defects.materiality: Transaction grouping directly concerns reliable multi-operation upload/replay, a selected first-comparison architecture. Leaving the available repair/version applicability unresolved weakens the required historical research and final interpretation.
final_material_defects.qualification: The final does not assert a current general PowerSync defect, and the omission does not prove the proposed domain design would fail. No future execution or deployment is required. The original captured view itself is unavailable; the historical maintainer comment predates the frozen run.
final_material_defects.confidence: HIGH for omitted source context; no claim of reproduced fix correctness

nonmaterial_findings_and_limits.finding: S16 calls the report’s React Native packages 1.25.x-era; the source’s actual package range is ^1.20.1 with RN 0.73.6. No current defect conclusion depends on this wording.
The photo contact-text/metadata rules are proposed controls, not demonstrated guarantees; review/sanitization details and platform policy are still to be chosen.

Deprecated/alpha attachment-helper and unsecured demo-server warnings are preserved in full source records but less visible in final prose. No helper or server is selected; the final requires independent application authorization and future platform checks.

Current SDK core implementation/test guesses could not be fetched (404/restricted/API 403); the evaluator inspected supplied sample code/callers, issue context and changelogs instead. No reconstruction or present-release correctness is certified.

critic_dispositions.note: Added a three-model access comparison with attribution, offboarding, offline-copy and fee tradeoffs.
Added cross-shift boundary, late arrivals and task/location/issue distinctions plus two-shift scenario.
Photo transforms, Wi-Fi default and deletion choices explicitly remain proposed and platform/policy dependent.
Queue order is per client; canonical claims, dedupe and current authorization remain app contracts.
Later assignments clear the current conflict view; app event history is separate.
Replicated branches differ from single-node 409; members are database-wide.
PostgreSQL guard is conditioned on schema/index/transaction; offline fairness is separate.
Storage can fail/evict; no post-eviction durability is promised.
At-access reporter caveats are appropriate, but S19 omits the existing explicit fix/version closure.
